text: The 2018 FIFA World Cup opening ceremony occurred on Thursday, 14 June 2018, at 3:30 BST (about half an hour before the opening match) at the Luzhniki Stadium in Moscow, Russia, where Russia defeated Saudi Arabia 5–0.[2][3] The official mascot of the tournament was Zabivaka (English: "The one who scores"), a wolf designed to represent fun, charm, and character, which was voted for by a 53% margin.[4] Former World Cup-winning Brazilian striker Ronaldo was also a mascot and was originally intended to deliver the ceremonial first kick, but instead, he passed the official match ball—an Adidas Telstar 18—to the child mascot Zabivaka, who then kicked it off to begin the tournament. The match ball was sent into space with the International Space Station crew in March and returned to Earth in early June.[5] Russian President Vladimir Putin delivered the opening speech, describing Russia as "open, hospitable and friendly" and emphasizing the unifying power of football, stating that it transcends language, ideology, or faith. He concluded by saying: “Our duty is to preserve this power of humanity for generations to come for the sake of developing sports and strengthening peace and mutual understanding between people. I wish all the teams’ success and an unforgettable experience for the fans. Welcome to Russia.” FIFA President Gianni Infantino followed with a speech stating: “Welcome to the FIFA World Cup here in Russia. As of today, for one month, football will conquer Russia and from Russia, football will conquer the world. Enjoy the biggest celebration on earth. Thank you President Putin, thank you Moscow, Spasibo [thank you] Russia.” After the speeches, the ceremony performances began before the Russia vs. Saudi Arabia match.[6][7][8] British pop singer Robbie Williams performed "Let Me Entertain You" and later sang "Feel" and a duet of "Angels" with Russian soprano Aida Garifullina, as performers emerged dressed in the flags of all 32 teams, each carrying a sign with their nation's name. Williams then performed "Rock DJ" in an encore as the pitch was cleared for the match.[9] During the encore, Williams gave the middle finger, prompting Fox in the US to issue an apology, while ITV in the UK had cut away before the incident.[10] While singing "Rock DJ," Williams altered the lyrics to "But I did this for free," replacing "Every night"—the reason for this change remains unexplained. Williams appeared on This Morning on 19 June, explaining that under pressure with only one minute left before kickoff, he performed a one-minute countdown using his middle finger, which he admitted he regrets and cannot trust himself to avoid. When asked if he regrets it, he said: "Yeah, of course, yeah. I cannot trust me. And the last thing I said to my manager before we sat down on the sofa here was, 'what could go wrong,' because I don't know what I'm going to do at any time. There's no, sort of, plan. The plan was, sing in key, don't fall over. That was the plan and 99% of the plan, I pulled off.” He added that nothing actually popped into his head, stating there was a block between him and sense, and only later realized he had done it. A total of 21 foreign heads of state attended the match, marking the largest gathering of leaders for a FIFA World Cup match.
